'''Uri Sivan''' ({{Langx|he|אורי סיון}}; born 1955) is an Israeli [[physicist]] who is the 17th president of the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]]. He is also the holder of the Bertoldo Badler Chair in the Technion's Faculty of Physics.

==Biography==
Uri Sivan's parents [[aliyah|immigrated]] to [[Mandatory Palestine]] from Poland in 1936.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Prof-Uri-Sivan-takes-office-as-President-of-Technion-603234|title=Prof. Uri Sivan takes office as President of Technion|work=The Jerusalem Post|date=September 29, 2019}}</ref> They studied at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] after being banned from European universities  because they were Jewish.<ref name="auto"/>

Sivan served as a pilot in the [[Israeli Air Force]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/technion-appoints-physicist-prof-uri-sivan-as-new-president/|title=Technion appoints physicist Prof. Uri Sivan as new president|date=June 24, 2019 |work= The Times of Israel}}</ref>

Sivan has a BSc in Physics and Mathematics, and an MSc and PhD in physics from [[Tel Aviv University]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://ats.org/news/professor-uri-sivan-elected-new-president-of-the-technion/|title=Professor Uri Sivan Elected New President of the Technion|website=ATS|date=February 7, 2019}}</ref>

Sivan lives in [[Haifa, Israel]].<ref name="auto"/> He is married and has three children.<ref name="auto"/>
==Academic career==
In 1991, after three years at [[IBM]]’s [[T. J. Watson Research Center]] in New York State, Sivan joined the Faculty of Physics at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, and became the holder of the Bertoldo Badler Chair.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto2"/>

Sivan set up and led the [[Russell Berrie Nanotechnology Institute|Russell Berrie Nanotechnology Research Institute]] at Technion from 2005 to 2010, and in 2017 he set up the National Advisory Committee for Quantum Science and Technology of the Council for Higher Education's Planning and Budgeting Committee.<ref name="auto2"/>

In September 2019, Sivan became the 17th President of the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, replacing [[Peretz Lavie]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto2"/>

==Awards and recognition==

Sivan was awarded the [[Israel Academy of Sciences]] Bergmann Prize, the Mifal Hapais Landau Prize for the Sciences and Research, the Rothschild Foundation Bruno Prize, the Technion's Hershel Rich Innovation Award, and the Taub Award for Excellence in Research.<ref name="auto1"/>
